rationale: This is a cosmetic template swap of the archive's "Liquidity-Funded Growth Short" (same P/S × high-capex × cash-depletion mechanism, MIN-of-ranks re-expressed as the now-standard IND_ZSCORE×INDICATOR gate already used three times in the archive), so it tests no new economic content and its negative FF5 alpha is likely the same effect re-measured.

It is a single-operand substitution on the archive's best signal that replaces the asset-*age* mechanism (ppent/ppegt) with a tangibility-mix change that is largely a mechanical restatement of high capex relative to asset growth, so it dilutes rather than extends the rejuvenation story and the claimed coverage gain from dropping ppegt is marginal.

Payout is a genuinely new theme for this pair and the internally consistent free-cash-flow coverage gate (oancf − capx − dvc > 0) is a substantive sustainability condition rather than a relabeled dividend-yield sort, though the ~payer-only universe will cut coverage sharply and the result should be checked against plain dividend yield within payers.

The investment leg is a genuinely distinct construct — co-movement of capex-intensity changes with internal cash-flow changes rather than the level, growth, or volatility of investment already tested — and the NEG(ABS(...)) direction correctly matches the stated positive expected sign, with the main risk being that small mismatches proxy for firms with little activity at all.

This is essentially the published glamour-acquirer anomaly (Rau–Vermaelen 1998; Loughran–Vijh 1997) — high-valuation acquirers underperform — and the COALESCE of aqc with goodwill deltas splices two differently scaled, sparsely populated variables whose zero/missing distinction will dominate the ranking.

The non-monotonic middle-band gate is correctly constructed (the indicator difference equals 1 only for the interior band) and the ex-ante hypothesis is coherent, but a 5-observation TS_RANK places quantile values exactly on the 0.25/0.75 thresholds, making the selected band knife-edge and potentially collapsing to a thin, unstable subsample.
